  • First and foremost he has a significantly worse offensive line. Here is a large look at projected offensive line and Seattle has done nothing to midigate the loses they've had or fill the holes they had last year. They grade out as possibly being the worse line in football and they have to face a pretty tough schedule of defensive lines. He had 6 games with a decent o-line (when Unger was healthy) and in those 6 games he tore it up for 23.3 ppg standard.   • Second biggest issue is that he isn't necessarily the goal line threat this year. Graham will give him some easier looks into the end zone, but he will take away alot of the chances he would have had the last few years.

  • Running backs decline at age 27, he is only 2 years past that, but it is something to note as he's had a huge amount of carries the last few years.

  • He has 3 years in a row of 310-340 touches, which when you have more than 300 carries you have a very good chance at regression the following year because of the wear of the body, so he does have a decent chance to wear down.

  • [Football Perspective took all running backs](I looked at all running backs who entered the league in 1990 or later, rushed for at least 5,000 rushing yards, averaged at least 40 rushing yards per game for their careers, and are retired. Add all this together and I'm not saying he is gonna bust at all. I think Lynch is still crazy good, but add all those points together and the fact he is facing a tough schedule for defensive lines and I think it pushes him to the RB10 area from the RB2-3 level.

I don't understand the hate for DNF. I mean, yeah, it didn't do anything groundbreaking in the FPS genre (who does these days?), but I don't remember it suffering from game-breaking bugs, for example. The game-play was pretty solid (discounting the loading times), it was colorful, the graphics were pretty good and a huge amount of attention was payed to the details (mini-games, interactions with the environment etc).

Obviously, it was full of tasteless, sexist, juvenile humor. But seriously, what did everyone else expect? It's Duke fucking-balls-of-steel Nukem. The whole character is meant to be a two-dimensional, shallow, parody of juvenile machismo. Duke Nukem is like a Chuck Norris joke made flesh and then blown-up with an atom bomb.

Criticizing Duke Nukem Forever for those things is like criticizing Postal for senseless violence or the WWF for the unrealistic portrayal of classic wrestling.

Furthermore, this criticism is doubly unfair in my mind as DNF is fully self-aware and at no point takes itself too seriously.

Edit: to be fair, I played the game a while after its release, so maybe my experience with the patched/fixed PC version might have been very different.

Level design was mostly uninspired linear corridor walking, so I'll not argue that the design was shitty overall, but at least you had things to interact with inside those levels.

The worst that can be said about the game is that it was mediocre in a lot of ways. The amount of content wasn't on the same level as a true AAA-title, it wasn't worth the hype and it definitely wasn't worth $50+ (I think I payed something like $5-6 on Steam) with its short playing time. But for all that, it was still fun and it wasn't a bad game worthy of all the hate directed at it. It was just a sort of OK.
